facts.title: The Initial Enrollment Period and when coverage starts
facts.question: When can I sign up for Medicare, and when does it start?
facts.text: The Initial Enrollment Period lasts 7 months: the 3 months before the month a person turns 65, that month, and the 3 months after. Someone who signs up before the month they turn 65 has Part B start that month; someone who signs up in the month they turn 65 or in the 3 months after has Part B start the next month. Premium-free Part A starts the month a person turns 65. Coverage always starts on the first of a month, and a birthday on the first of the month counts as the month before.
facts.summary: The Initial Enrollment Period is the 3 months before the month a person turns 65, that month, and the 3 months after; signing up in or after the birthday month starts Part B the next month.

facts.title: COBRA and signing up for Part B
facts.question: I have COBRA. Can I wait to sign up for Part B?
facts.text: COBRA isn’t coverage from a current job, so it doesn’t let someone put off Part B without a penalty, and it doesn’t create a later Special Enrollment Period. People on COBRA who are turning 65 generally sign up for Part A and Part B during their Initial Enrollment Period.
facts.summary: COBRA isn’t coverage from a current job, so people on COBRA who are turning 65 generally sign up for Part A and Part B during their Initial Enrollment Period.

sources.label: CMS: 5 things you need to know about signing up for Medicare

facts.title: COBRA pays second once someone is 65
facts.question: Does COBRA still pay my bills once I'm eligible for Medicare?
facts.text: Once someone is 65 and eligible for Medicare, Medicare pays first and COBRA pays second. COBRA may pay only a small part of a bill, so without Part B a person can be left paying most of the cost.
facts.summary: Once someone is 65, Medicare pays first and COBRA pays second, so without Part B a person can be left paying most of a bill.

facts.title: The Medigap Open Enrollment Period
facts.question: When can I buy a Medigap policy?
facts.text: The Medigap Open Enrollment Period is a one-time 6 months that starts the month Part B starts for someone 65 or older. During it, an insurer can’t turn a person down or charge more because of their health. After it, an insurer can ask health questions and may decline or charge more.
facts.summary: The Medigap Open Enrollment Period is a one-time 6 months starting the month Part B starts at 65 or older; after it an insurer can ask health questions.

facts.title: Ozempic and similar medicines: prior authorization
facts.question: Will a drug plan cover Ozempic?
facts.text: Medicare drug plans generally cover Ozempic for type 2 diabetes, and many require prior authorization: the plan’s approval, requested by the prescriber, before it pays. Medicare drug plans don’t cover a drug prescribed only for weight loss.
facts.summary: Medicare drug plans generally cover Ozempic for type 2 diabetes and many require prior authorization, the plan’s approval requested by the prescriber; they don’t cover a drug prescribed only for weight loss.
